statement: Fill the area enclosed by objects around a picked internal point using a pattern, solid color or gradient, applying island detection and a gap tolerance to find the boundary.
superiority: Boundary detection is exact with repair preview.

acceptance.sketch: Pick inside a 10x10 square with a circle hole r=2: hatch region area = 100 - pi*4 for Normal island style; gap tolerance 0.05 closes a 0.04 gap.

notes: Verified against help page "HATCH (Command)". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-006BE8D3-0731-47BA-A7CF-1B50282CD108 | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Hatch; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row.

statement: Define a hatch boundary by selecting objects that enclose an area; interior objects are not detected automatically and must be selected to be treated according to the island detection style.

notes: Verified against help page "Common Options (Hatch and Gradient Dialog Box)". statement: The program must provide FILL with On and Off options that switch hatches, 2D solid objects, and wide polylines between solid rendering and outline-only rendering on screen and in plots, taking effect on existing objects after a regen and leaving lineweight display unaffected.

acceptance.sketch: Draw a wide polyline, run FILL Off then REGEN and assert only its outline is rendered/plotted; run FILL On then REGEN and assert it is filled again.

notes: Added from help page "FILL (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide GRADIENT to fill a closed region or chosen objects with a smooth one- or two-color blend, using the Hatch Creation ribbon tab, or the Hatch and Gradient dialog when HPDLGMODE is 1.

acceptance.sketch: Draw a closed circle, run GRADIENT, click inside it and accept, and assert a gradient hatch object is created that is bounded by the circle.

notes: Added from help page "GRADIENT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide -HATCH as the command-line form of hatching, filling an area found from internal points or selected objects with a predefined, custom, user-defined, solid, or gradient fill, with options to set properties and pattern names, draw or remove boundaries, advanced boundary and island detection settings, and to generate separate lines rather than a hatch object when the pattern is prefixed with an asterisk.

acceptance.sketch: Run -HATCH, choose Properties ANSI31 scale 1 angle 0, pick an internal point of a closed rectangle and assert an associative hatch with pattern ANSI31 is created inside; repeat with '*ANSI31' and assert plain lines are produced instead.

notes: Added from help page "-HATCH (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide -HATCHEDIT to modify existing hatches or fills from the command line, including disassociating, changing island style (Ignore, Outer, Normal), replacing properties like pattern name, scale factor, and rotation angle, assigning draw order, and other hatch-specific options depending on the object type.

acceptance.sketch: Create an associative hatch, run -HATCHEDIT Disassociate and assert the hatch no longer updates when its boundary is stretched; run Properties to change scale to 2 and assert spacing doubles.

notes: Added from help page "-HATCHEDIT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: REVCLOUDPROPERTIES must change the approximate arc chord length of a selected revision cloud, with the default derived from the first cloud in the drawing and uniform or varying arcs controlled by REVCLOUDARCVARIANCE.

acceptance.sketch: Select a revision cloud with arc length 0.5, run REVCLOUDPROPERTIES and enter 1.0; the cloud is rebuilt with arcs of about 1.0 chord length.

notes: Added from help page "REVCLOUDPROPERTIES (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must ship standard hatch pattern libraries in PAT files (metric and imperial, LT variants) and load user PAT files with a header line of asterisk, name (max 31 chars) and description followed by descriptor lines of angle, origin, delta offsets and dash lengths.

source.ref: About Custom Hatch Patterns and Hatch Pattern Definitions

acceptance.sketch: Scenario: load a PAT file with '*ANSI31, ANSI Iron' and '45, 0,0, 0,.125', hatch a rectangle and expect 45-degree lines spaced 0.125 apart perpendicular to the line direction.

notes: Added from help page "About Custom Hatch Patterns and Hatch Pattern Definitions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must support PAT patterns composed of several definition lines with differing angles, non-zero origins and offsets, so each line family is positioned independently and the combined pattern (such as AR-B816 or an inverted-U) tiles correctly.

source.ref: About Hatch Patterns With Multiple Lines

acceptance.sketch: Scenario: define *IUS with three descriptor lines (90, 0 and 270 degrees) and hatch a square; expect repeating inverted-U shapes with a 1-unit repeat.

notes: Added from help page "About Hatch Patterns With Multiple Lines"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must interpret dash lengths in hatch pattern lines (positive is drawn, negative is a gap, zero is a dot, up to six per line, cycling from the origin) and apply the delta-x shift and delta-y spacing for offsetting successive lines.

source.ref: About Hatch Patterns with Dashed Lines

acceptance.sketch: Scenario: define *DDOT45 as '45, 0,0, 0,.5, .5,-.25, 0,-.25', hatch an area and expect a repeating dash, gap, dot, gap sequence on 45-degree lines spaced 0.5 apart.

notes: Added from help page "About Hatch Patterns with Dashed Lines"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Hatch must fill enclosed areas or objects with predefined, user-defined or custom (acad.pat style) patterns, solid fills or gradient fills (tint, shade or two-color), including pattern libraries from other vendors, and allow creating new boundaries.

acceptance.sketch: Hatch a closed rectangle with ANSI31 and assert hatch lines appear; hatch it with a two-color gradient and assert both colors are stored.

notes: Added from help page "About Hatch Patterns and Fills"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Hatch scale must be settable manually (HPSCALE) or automatically per viewport through annotative hatches, with HPMAXLINES and HPMAXAREAS limiting excessive line and area counts and overly sparse hatches degrading to solid.

acceptance.sketch: Set HPSCALE=2 and assert new hatches use spacing doubled; create an annotative hatch and assert it renders at different scales in two viewports; set HPMAXLINES low and assert a dense hatch is refused.

notes: Added from help page "About Hatch Pattern Scaling"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: A wipeout must be a polygonal region masking underlying objects with the background color, with a frame that can be toggled for editing and plotting, usable on layouts in paper space over model space, and plotted like a raster image (requiring Plot Paper Space Last cleared).

statement: Revision clouds must be closed polylines of arcs created by dragging or by converting circles, ellipses, closed polylines or splines, with a calligraphy style, varying or uniform arc chord length (REVCLOUDARCVARIANCE) and grip editing controlled by REVCLOUDGRIPS.

acceptance.sketch: Convert a closed polyline to a revision cloud and assert it consists of arc segments; set REVCLOUDARCVARIANCE off and assert all arc chords are equal.
